text:
Tomas: Hey team, got a refurbished MBP from ops and enrolled it, but FileVault is already On and the MDM console is rejecting the escrow with an error 'recovery key owned by different MDM tenant'. Can't get a local dev environment until that's fixed. Anyone seen this?

Rina (IT): Welcome! Yeah that happens when a device was previously assigned to a different org and the old recovery was escrowed there. Can you paste `fdesetup status` and `sudo profiles status -type enrollment` and the device serial (`system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep Serial`) so I can look it up?

Tomas: Here you go:
```
$ fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
Users enabled for FileVault:
 - prevuser

$ sudo profiles status -type enrollment
Enrolled: Yes
Profile identifier: com.redwood.mdm.enroll
Last check-in: 2027-01-12T08:14:01Z
Device compliance: pending (escrow conflict)

$ system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep Serial
  Serial Number (system): C02T8XYZLVD7
```
I was expecting the device to be wiped first but ops said it's ready-to-assign.

Device Bot: Device C02T8XYZLVD7: enrolled=true, supervised=true, last_owner=acme-ops-old, escrow_status=escrowed_to_tenant:acme-old-org, reassignable=false (needs wipe or owner-release).

Rina (IT): Thanks. Because the recovery key is escrowed to a different tenant we can't rotate or replace the escrow in place. Two options: 1) Ask the previous tenant to release the escrow (not possible here), or 2) securely wipe the device and re-enroll it into our tenant. Since it's supervised, a wipe + DEP reassign is the recommended flow.

Cal (Manager): Ops confirmed they pulled these units from another org's pool. Sorry, that was a mistake on our inventory side. Tomas, please back up any personal files (if any) then IT will schedule a remote wipe and re-provision.

Tomas: No personal files, I already have my dev stuff in the cloud. Wipe away.

Rina (IT): Ok scheduling secure wipe now. I'll push a Lock & Erase command; you'll get a modal saying "This device will be erased and re-enrolled to Redwood Inference". After wipe you'll follow the DEP setup assistant. Expect a short window where the Mac boots to Setup Assistant.

Device Bot: Issuing Erase Device command for C02T8XYZLVD7. Expected action: user confirm on-device (if required) or automatic erase if MDM has erase permission. Reassign will occur post-erase.

Tomas: Getting the confirmation dialog now, confirming. It's starting the erase.

Tomas: Rebooted into Setup Assistant, completed DEP enrollment. Ran checks:
```
$ sudo profiles status -type enrollment
Enrolled: Yes
Profile identifier: com.redwood.mdm.enroll
Last check-in: 2027-01-12T09:02:12Z
Device compliance: pending (FileVault enabling)

$ fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.
No user is enabled for FileVault.
```

Rina (IT): Pushing FileVault enable (institutional escrow) now. You should see the prompt to allow Redwood Device Management to enable FileVault using the organization's recovery key. Accept and enter your password.

Device Bot: Pushing FileVault enable (institutional escrow) for C02T8XYZLVD7.

Tomas: Accepted prompt, entered password, rebooted.

Tomas: Post-reboot `fdesetup status` shows: 
```
FileVault is On.
Users enabled for FileVault:
 - tomas
```
All good, Docker installed, dev environment up. Thanks Rina/ops!

Rina (IT): Closing notes for channel: if you get a refurbished device that still has FileVault enabled and the escrow points to another tenant, a wipe and reassign is required. Always confirm with ops that devices are factory reset before assignment. Tag IT if you need us to handle the wipe.

Cal (Manager): Thanks everyone, lesson learned for ops inventory tagging :facepalm: Congrats Tomas and welcome aboard!"
